correctness.rationale: Exact uniform-edge Markov dynamics plus the degree-two complement guarantee only zero or two vacancies. A tagged forbidden edge obeys a transition ratio \(1+O(k^{-2})\) relative to the one-missing-edge model; the telescoping product is \((K^2-1)/(N^2-1)\). Joint survival of any 3 or 4 prescribed vertices bounds the conditional chance of another forbidden edge at cutoff K by \(O(K/N+K^2/N)\). Exceptional paths have uniformly \(O(K^{-2})\) final tagged survival. \(K\asymp N^{1/3}\) yields \(3(N^2-1)^{-1}(1+O(N^{-1/3}))\) for every forbidden edge, then disjoint summation yields the claim. A standalone rational-DP script checks 13 instances, and independent 9! edge-order enumeration checks one instance; numerical evidence is supplementary only.

originality.rationale: The uniform theorem for arbitrary forbidden paths, cycles and nonregular degree-two complements is not implied by the already recorded perfect-matching-deletion special case. Full accessible principal papers study fixed host degree/large girth, sparse random hosts, or oblivious decision-order approximations, rather than the rare two-vacancy law on a dense host with degree-two deleted graph. The novel structural element is an architecture-insensitive leading coefficient with a uniform error bound. Older restricted-access texts leave specific unresolved bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: The problem distinguishes feasible perfect coverage from rare irreversible jamming, a quantity invisible in limiting adsorption density. The universal leading amplitude is independent of path/cycle location, forbidding-cluster geometry, and regularity, providing a structural theorem for an infinite family not recoverable by mere substitution into the previously recorded deleted-matching result. The uniform error supplies a quantitative reliability scale. The theorem does not assert physical equilibrium or second-order laws.
